ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OM$ is the bisector of $\angle AOC$, and $ON$ is the bisector of $\angle BOC$. As shown in Figure 1, when $\angle AOB$ is a right angle and $\angle BOC=60^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle MON$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle AOB=90^\circ$ and $\angle BOC=60^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle AOC=\angle AOB+\angle BOC=90^\circ+60^\circ=150^\circ$. \\
Since $OM$ bisects $\angle AOC$ and $ON$ bisects $\angle BOC$, \\
thus $\angle MOC=\frac{1}{2}\angle AOC=75^\circ$ and $\angle NOC=\frac{1}{2}\angle BOC=30^\circ$. \\
Therefore, $\angle MON=\angle MOC-\angle NOC=75^\circ-30^\circ=\boxed{45^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: There are three small diagrams in the figure, and the problem specifies using the left-side Figure 1. In Figure 1, all rays emanate from point O, OA is vertically upward, OB is horizontally to the right, OM is between OA and OB, ON is between OB and OC, and OC is at the lower right; from Figure 1 it can be read that in the clockwise direction they are approximately OA, OM, OB, ON, OC. Then reason: According to the specified method, set the direction of OB as 0°. Because ∠AOB is a right angle, the direction of OA is +90°. Also because ∠BOC=60° and OC is below OB, the direction of OC is -60°. OM bisects ∠AOC, so the direction of OM is (+90°+(-60°))/2=+15°. ON bisects ∠BOC, so the direction of ON is (0°+(-60°))/2=-30°. Therefore ∠MON=15°-(-30°)=45°.
